items.title: Iola Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Wilton, CT, July 17, 2011
items.q: He and Paul had an agreement. The rhythm section would be guaranteed a salary.

ctx.x: And did he pay the other three guys before he paid himself?

He and Paul had an agreement. The rhythm section would be guaranteed a salary. And the agreement with Paul was — I don’t remember the exact amount, whether it was 40 percent or 50 percent or what it was, whatever the gross was, I’ve forgotten just what the percentage was. So sometimes it ended up that Dave ended up with very little. Because he was paying the transportation, the commissions, and that sort of thing.

Well I’ve gotten the sense over the years that he has used you as an opinion and a sounding board about some of his work. When I was here ten years ago he was working on a piece. Unfortunately it was the beginning of the Afghanistan war, and he was working on a piece that I believe he said the text encouraged women not have children because the times were so awful. And you told him nobody’s going to want to sing that, it’s too sad. And it made me think that you’re fairly forthright with your opinions about his…
